driver: An intervention can act on a case only from a start that waits on a hand-off whose delay differs case by case and unit by unit, so the outcomes it can remove are the ones that fall after that start; a trial's effect measured over the whole window at a unit where the hand-off is quick, carried as one ratio to units where it is slow, credits the slow units with outcomes that happen before the intervention could begin.
driver_concrete: Each maternity unit's expected readmissions avoided is the trial's reduction in readmissions after the first outreach visit applied to the unit's own eligible readmissions that came after the day following the community office's receipt of the baby's discharge notification, not the trial's 28-day intention-to-treat ratio applied to all of a unit's readmissions; Ravensby Royal's and St Aldric's notifications often reach the office days late, so many of their early jaundice and feeding readmissions fall before any visit could happen.
stump: The default path carries the trial's 28-day intention-to-treat ratio to every eligible readmission at each unit, so Ravensby Royal and St Aldric's are credited with readmissions that fall before a nurse could reach the baby and the posts and the readmissions avoided both come out wrong.

differentiation.task309: 309 reads an effect class by class of an event's intensity and carries it to a forward set; here no effect varies by any class of case: the effect is constant once the service starts, and what moves is how much of each case's window the service can reach, set per case by a hand-off recorded in a second file.
differentiation.task105: 105 v1's lead time was one filed season for one class of commitment against one opening date; here each case's start comes from its own receipt time in a separate log, and the trial's effect has to be re-based before it is carried.
differentiation.task127: 127's first architecture counts the units a capacity-limited team can finish before a period closes; here no capacity binds the decisive step: each case's start is set by its own hand-off time in a second file, and what is counted is how many of a unit's outcomes fall after that start.
differentiation.task259: 259 ages reported levels to a reference date by a trend read within units; here nothing is aged: each case's outcome counts only if it falls after the case's own start, recorded in a separate log, and a trial's effect is re-based on that window before it is carried.
